claims.text: Ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder initially forms a simple BCC solid solution.
SPS at 1000 °C produces a dense microstructure in MgAlTiVFeCo.
SPS at 1000 °C produces uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases.
The dense microstructure and distributed barrier oxide phases enhance mechanical strength.
The dense microstructure and distributed barrier oxide phases enhance corrosion resistance.
The dense microstructure and distributed barrier oxide phases enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
These improvements can be achieved while maintaining low alloy density.
High temperature and pressure during SPS provide sufficient diffusion to form a continuous passive film.
The continuous passive film blocks chloride-ion penetration.
Blocking chloride-ion penetration produces high polarization resistance and improved corrosion resistance.
Oxidation of the 1000 °C SPS material at 900 °C in air follows diffusion-controlled parabolic kinetics.
The oxidation process exhibits a biphasic growth pattern.
Samples sintered at 1000 °C will reach approximately 96.7% relative density.
Samples sintered at 1000 °C will reach approximately 1235 HV microhardness.
Samples sintered at 850–950 °C will have less than 96.7% relative density and lower microhardness than samples sintered at 1000 °C.
Samples sintered at 1000 °C will have a lower oxidation rate than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
In 3.5 wt% NaCl, samples sintered at 1000 °C will show more positive corrosion potentials and lower current densities than lower-temperature samples.
Sintering above 1000 °C may cause magnesium volatilization.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient energy for densification and barrier-phase formation.
